venues.name: CC Atlanta
venues.narrative: **CCATL — Friday 11/20 (MOD MKZ/JK; entered by Mya; posted 2:53am ET 11/21)** Net $5,456 vs target $7,172 (76.1%). Food $350; no events; comps $119.75 (2.2%). 200 guests; check avg $27.28. Friday before Thanksgiving with a quiet start to the day — holidays can be unpredictable with guests' vacations and breaks. The opener used the down time to connect with guests and ABK the bar, and was cut a little before 8pm. A flow of guests started around 9pm; the closer followed right in and set the tone with great music. Coaching note: get out from behind the bar to manicure tables and interact with guests. Quiet night overall; hoping for more action Saturday. Kitchen: smooth night. No events; no maintenance needs; no incidents; no-shows not charged. Highlight: getting to talk to guests more than usual.

venues.name: CC Nashville
venues.narrative: **CCNSH — Friday 11/20 (MOD KK, Chef Rick; entered by BT; posted 3:49am ET 11/21)** Net $8,821 vs target $10,281 (85.8%). Food $369; no events; comps $99 (1.12%). 299 guests; check avg $29.50. A somewhat slow Friday — the MOD (only half joking) blames the GTA 6 release. Still some great guests in: several parties of 10 or more and a couple of celebrations, but never much of a pop. At about midnight the fire alarm went off; after a few minutes the team started handing out plastic cups so guests could take their drinks as the bar evacuated. Just as people were starting to leave the alarm shut off and security confirmed there was no fire. Most guests stayed, but it put a damper on the evening. Kitchen: smooth sailing with Rick. 86 ponies. No events; no maintenance needs; no incident logged on the form; no-shows not charged. Highlight: a guest ordering a 'dirty martini on nickels' — which turned out to be the tab name, not a new serve.

venues.name: D&C Denver
venues.weather: Nice evening for late fall; not too chilly
venues.narrative: **DVR — Friday 11/20 (AM MOD Evan -> Maggie S, Chef Lucas; PM MOD Evan F, Chef Lucas; entered by Evan F; posted 3:12am ET 11/21 — date field typed as 11/21, matched to Friday 11/20 by post time and day of week)** Net $11,952.72 incl. events; daily target entered as '???' on the form, so no target recorded. AM (coffee) $939.17, D&C PM $11,043.42, Garden/6A n/a; no event sales. Food incl. events $1,921.00. Comps $237.93 (~1.99%). 308 guests (Tock); check avg $38.81 (net incl. events / guests). AM: Friday was a slow roll until the last hour, which had a light cocktail fling; fresh batch of cold brew is live. PM: started off pretty slow but picked up around 7pm and persisted until shortly before close; lots of wine bottles going out, which was nice to see. Kitchen: pretty low-key night; all cast irons scrubbed and seasoned by Chef Lucas, pipes behind the left burners scrubbed and the grill scraped down. Break make-up complete. No incidents; no-shows not charged; no maintenance needs at the moment. Highlight: bartenders competing over who gets to take rail guests, and seeing regulars.

venues.name: D&C East Village
venues.narrative: **EV — Friday 11/20 (MOD Kyler, Chef Steves; entered by Sean; posted 10:39am ET 11/21)** Net $7,626 vs target $8,214 (92.8%). Food $700, beverage $6,926; retail $0; no event sales; comps $161 (2.1%) — a couple of members, a few gifts, several DNLs. 249 guests (SevenRooms); check avg $30.63 (net/guests; form $31). Slow start that only went full Friday mode at around 7:30. A lot of quick rounds earlier in the night, which led to several tables clearing all at the same time. Strong middle with a few larger parties keeping the room's energy high, but ultimately finished with a pretty mellow room. Top sellers: Burner Phone, Rosalie, Shinebox. Kitchen: no notes. Door: a very warm night for mid-November; started strong with a solid 6pm push and a waitlist from around 8pm that stayed long all night with a mix of 2s and small groups; full until about midnight. Fans from Denver came in, and lots of patient folks chatted at the door while tables were flipped. The end of the night brought some chaos with a group of 5 taking over the bar and a small line forming of people trying to get in before last call. Lexi made an appearance, as did some LA VIPs. One no-show (a 2-top at 9:45); no-shows charged. Menu count 20/20. Breakage: none.

venues.name: D&C Los Angeles
venues.weather: A cold night in the city
venues.narrative: **LA — Friday 11/20 (MOD/Chef Gigi + Julian + Joe + Josh + Angel; entered by Joe; posted 6:45am ET 11/21)** Net $12,102 vs target $11,925 (101.5%). Marquee $9,198; Standing Room $2,904. Food $2,159. Comps $374 (3.1%; staff food, member/VIP guests, birthday, anniversary, lots of DNL). 313 guests; check avg $90.32 as reported. A relatively steady Friday night: started with 127 covers on the books and a nice push right after open. The room filled not long after 7pm, just in time to open Standing Room. A small lull around 8pm let the team catch up on prep for the upcoming menu. The rest of the night was very steady but never overwhelming; flow of service was great and guests were excited to be there. The floor team made sure everyone was in good hands and every table was ABK'd. The last few hours mellowed out, making for a very smooth last call. Kitchen: everything came out looking great. No incidents; no-shows charged. Highlight: all the snacks and food the team brought in.

venues.name: D&C Washington DC
venues.narrative: **DC — Friday 11/20 (MOD Marcus / Josh; entered by Josh; posted 4:02am ET 11/21)** Net $9,178.49 incl. events vs target $10,424 (88.1%). Marquee bar $7,588.38; Garden $1,851.86; total sales $9,440.24. Food $900.00. Comps $261.75 (2.9%; friends & family and service recovery moments); voids n/a. 215 guests; guest check avg $37.93 and check avg $84.29 as reported. Garden: light start, didn't pick up until around 7:45–8pm; a handful of two-tops but mostly larger parties who joined the waitlist and then liked it outside so much they didn't want to move to the marquee. Once the team found its groove service ran smoothly — drinks out fast, bartenders splitting order-taking and food running. Foot traffic steady 9–11:30pm, died off by midnight; last call and garden closed. D&C: slower foot traffic to start, picking up around 7pm when the room filled and every table was seated; good mix of reservations and walk-ins before dinner. Alley traffic noticeably lighter than a typical Friday, likely as guests begin holiday travel. Pacing was solid and the team worked through the waitlist despite a few lingering tables. Floor service was okay but continues to fall short on clearing tables, water service and running food — the MOD wants more intentional, attentive section work. Bar top performed well with regular rounds and every guest acknowledged; service got harder after the barback was sent home sick, but it was manageable. A steady Friday with several familiar faces. Kitchen: slower night with limited orders; uptick in fingerling potatoes and fried chicken during the rush; both chefs stepped out to run food. Kitchen close not checked. Went well: pacing, regulars, round building, ticket passing, chefs running food. Do better: steps of service, giving guests the right of way, saying 'corner', back bar suggestions. No incidents; no-shows not charged; no-show revenue $0. Maintenance: curtains. Highlight: a friend of the bar popping in.

venues.name: Municipal Grand F&B
venues.narrative: **MG — Friday 11/20 (AM MOD Sam, Chef Lex; PM MOD James, Chef Drew; entered by Alexis; posted 1:45am ET 11/21)** Net $9,169 vs target $10,629 (86.3%). Municipal Bar AM $1,619, PM $5,252; Hot Eye $2,229; Sun Club $0 (closed). Food $2,738; no events; comps $92 (1.0%). Guests 183 (OpenTable: 26 morning + 157 evening); check avg $50.10 (net / guests). Morning: sleepy and slow on an expectedly slow weekend; a couple of food tours, nothing else remarkable. Evening: very slow compared to recent nights, mostly explained by the weather and time of year; the pop came in the 7 o'clock hour with a sharp drop after. Guests were quality for the most part and the vibe at the bar was great; easy end to the night with everyone out fairly early despite being down one closer. Hot Eye: a pretty tame Friday — steady from the beginning and all evening but never fully filled; a bachelorette group danced from 9pm to close along with other out-of-town groups; the 8pm bartender was cut around 10:30pm due to the slow pace. Kitchen: steady night, slow start, picked up around 7:30pm; good ticket times, no send-backs or complaints, no lows or 86s — solid Friday service. No incidents. Highlight: the groups in Hot Eye living their best lives.

venues.name: D&C Seattle
venues.weather: High of 47, lows around 36; foggy but no rain, chilly
venues.narrative: **SEA — Friday 11/20 (MOD Curtis; entered by Frank; posted 4:38am ET 11/21)** Net $10,914 vs target $10,801 (101.0%). Food $2,068; no events; comps $253.34 (2.3%; a few members/investors, F&F discounts, a couple of DNLs and service recoveries). 219 guests; avg guest spend $49.84. Weather chilly and foggy but the people still came out. Good start to the weekend: got going right away with a lot of first-timers early and some members/investors sprinkled in. Hit the usual 6–7pm lull; after late shifters clocked on, the team used the time to catch up and get everyone's breaks done. Staff meal was fantastic and up early enough to eat on breaks. After the pre-dinner lull the night settled into a constant, steady groove that was never overwhelming; one team member was cut at a decent time, the team handled the late-night pop very well, and the MOD also got out at a decent time. Kitchen: continues to pump food out and blow past sales goals. 86 Cointreau, Awayuki gin; low Hendrick's, Hampden Estate, Fino Romate, Daiyame Shochu, Taittinger, Heart of Stone Sour. No events; no maintenance needs; no incidents; no-shows charged. Highlight: two industry superfans visiting from Portland for a birthday, in two nights running — the whole team's thoughtful hospitality made it a truly special experience.
